purpose: The OPERATIONAL view: what a driver may rely on, right now, on this host. Kept separate from primitives/harness-matrix.json, which is aesop's historical PRODUCT-support matrix pinned at a stated commit and is not rewritten here. Each capability carries three independent answers -- does the product support it, has polytropos implemented it, has anyone verified it by running it -- because collapsing them into one boolean is how a driver comes to believe it holds a control it does not.
unknown_is_valid: A capability nobody has run reports verified=unknown, and a caller needing certainty must treat that as no. Filling these in optimistically would make the file worse than not having it.

dispatch.note: one authorized live invocation, scoped to validating flag handling; tests never invoke the real CLI

durable_attempts.note: polytropos capability, not a product one: every dispatch is recorded before and after it runs, a dead run's open attempt is closed as unknown and reconciled by re-running the check, budget usage carries across runs, tasks are claimed with O_EXCL. Exercised with stub executables and temp stores only; never run against the live CLI, so verified stays unknown

tool_pin.note: the `--allowedTools=<space-joined>` form is REQUIRED: the variadic form swallows the following positional, which silently consumed the prompt on every review dispatch. This row is why the registry has a verified column

confined_verify.note: polytropos capability, not a product one: verify commands run under an OS boundary. macOS only -- enforced mode refuses on Linux and Windows rather than downgrading

confined_dispatch.note: sandbox-exec blocks Keychain access and subscription credentials live there, so a confined dispatch reports 'Not logged in'. Keychain access is gated by entitlements, not profile rules; granting mach-lookup and keychain writes does not change it

status.note: no run-status query is implemented here, and whether the CLI exposes one has not been checked

cancel.note: the process tree can be terminated; that says nothing about whether the model call it made was already billed

independent_review.note: phase-end review dispatched with a restricted permission profile and recorded in the attempt ledger. Never run against the live CLI from this repository, so verified stays unknown

extended_roles.note: the seven optional roles (scout, test-author, second-verifier, red-team, security-auditor, docs-editor, synthesizer) are sequenced only by the interactive execute skill; `run` is one task, one role, with no hook sequencing, so a kit that declares one is refused or disclosed before dispatch (--roster-gap)

concurrent_dispatch.note: no adapter yet: bin/claude_execute.py keeps its own sequential loop; bin/kit_scheduler.py dispatches through harness adapters (stub, cursor) only

workflow_evaluation.note: bin/workflow_eval.py claude adapter: repo_bench's claude argv for implement, a restricted-permission dispatch for review, dollars from data/pricing.json; never run live from this repository

Exercised with stub executables and temp stores only; never run against the live CLI, so verified stays unknown

sandbox_read_only.note: review and acceptance are pinned read-only and extra arguments cannot override it. The flag's runtime effect has not been verified here

structured_events.note: thread.started / item.completed / turn.completed are parsed; model attestation falls back to unknown when no correlated record appears

async_tools.note: tool calls the model does not block on, returned later under the original call id. Reported for the vendor's API and not checked here against vendor documentation; whether `codex exec` exposes it has not been checked either, and nothing in this repo uses it. Recorded so a scheduler cannot assume it

mid_turn_steering.note: new user instructions injected into a running turn with finished work kept. Reported for a persistent API connection; the driver runs `codex exec` to completion and has no channel to steer through, so this is unsupported here whatever the product does

effort_per_turn.note: changing reasoning effort between turns of one session with the cached prefix intact. Distinct from per-dispatch effort, which the driver sets once on the command line before the run starts and never changes afterwards

cursor.modes_note: IDE agent, local CLI, and background/cloud agents are three products; this registry describes the CLI, which bin/cursor_adapter.py drives. Files it installs (.cursor/skills, .cursor/agents) are read by all three, which says nothing about driving the other two -- see cursor_adapter.modes_report.

dispatch.note: bin/cursor_execute.py run through bin/cursor_adapter.build_dispatch; never invoked live from this repository -- tests stub the binary -- so verified stays unknown

identity_probe.note: polytropos capability: the generically named `agent` is dispatched to only after `--version` or `about --format json` names Cursor; unknown fails closed. The probe's output format is undocumented, so which of the two answers positively on a real install is unverified

read_only_dispatch.note: review and verification dispatches pass --mode ask and never --force; whether ask mode refuses every write is the product's promise, not verified here

model_selection.note: --model is passed as written; the host's list is read at run time and never mirrored into a pricing file

structured_events.note: the output schema is undocumented: a top-level object is kept and only a string `model` field is read as an observed model; everything else stays unknown

status.note: `status` reports authentication, not a run; `ls`/`resume` address chats. No per-run status is exposed, so the adapter raises CapabilityError

cancel.note: no documented way to cancel a run from outside it; bin/proc_runner.py can stop the process tree, which says nothing about whether the call was billed

cli_sandbox.note: Cursor's own command sandbox is documented and not relied on: verification runs under bin/exec_policy.py, and the dispatch itself is unconfined, as on every harness

usage_report.note: the CLI documents no usage or cost output; state.vscdb is an undocumented SQLite store this repository does not open; every Cursor dispatch is unpriced (usd null)

skill_files.note: the bundle installs one project-scoped skill through the ownership-aware installer; discovery by the product is not verified here

subagent_files.source: https://cursor.com/docs/subagents (.cursor/agents/*.md: name, description, model, readonly, is_background)
subagent_files.note: the bundle installs an implementer and a readonly verifier; the driver does not dispatch subagents itself

ide_mode.note: the IDE agent reads the installed files; no adapter operation drives the IDE

cloud_mode.note: cloud subagents and private workers read project-level files only; no adapter operation launches or drives one
